claims.statement: utils/cautils/acme_flow.go exposes ACMECreateCertFlow (subject, certFile, keyFile args plus --san; builds the flow with withSubjectSANs and withProvisionerName, calls GetCertificate, writes the PEM chain with writeCert, and serializes the private key unless it is a TPM/attestation key) and ACMESignCSRFlow (same transaction using a caller-provided CSR via withCSR, writing only the certificate file).

step ca certificate dispatches to ACME: when --acme is set and no token is given it calls cautils.ACMECreateCertFlow(ctx, ""), and when GenerateToken returns the ACMETokenError type (carrying the ACME provisioner name, also returned by OfflineCA for ACME provisioners) it calls ACMECreateCertFlow with that provisioner name.

newACMEFlow rejects offline mode as mutually exclusive with ACME, rejects --standalone combined with --webroot, forces standalone on when neither is set, and derives the ACME directory as <ca-url>/acme/<provisioner>/directory when --acme is absent (requiring a provisioner name).

getClientTruststoreOption uses --root if set, else the default root at pki.GetRootCAPath() if present; when merging is requested (explicit --acme) it appends the local root to the system cert pool with a TLS 1.2-minimum transport, otherwise it uses ca.WithRootFile or the default transport.

createNewOrderRequest validates SANs for ACME (email and URI SANs rejected; wildcard DNS names rejected because DNS validation is not implemented), and for LetsEncrypt directories rejects not-before/not-after and always adds the subject CN as a DNS identifier; otherwise it builds a NewOrderRequest with NotBefore/NotAfter from flags.ParseTimeDuration and adds the subject as a DNS or IP identifier if absent.

HTTP-01 challenge serving has two modes behind the issueMode interface: standaloneMode starts an HTTP server on --http-listen (default :80) serving /.well-known/acme-challenge/<token> with the key authorization and shuts it down on cleanup; webrootMode writes the key authorization to <webroot>/.well-known/acme-challenge/<token> (0755 dir, 0644 file) served by an existing webserver and removes it on cleanup.

serveAndValidateHTTPChallenge runs the selected mode, calls ac.ValidateChallenge, sleeps 1s, then getChallengeStatus polls every 5 seconds until the challenge is validated or failed, extracting detailed error messages from the challenge object.

authorizeOrder iterates the order's AuthorizationURLs and validates each identifier with http-01 via serveAndValidateHTTPChallenge (unless attesting) or with device-attest-01 via doDeviceAttestation (when --attestation-uri is set); it errors if no challenge for an identifier can be validated.

finalizeOrder polls the order up to 10 times at 1s intervals until status 'ready', calls ac.FinalizeOrder with the CSR, then polls again until status 'valid', erroring with the order state if either phase times out.

acmeFlow.GetCertificate builds the order (identifiers, or a single permanent-identifier when --attestation-uri is set), creates the ACME order, authorizes it, generates a CSR when none was provided (key from kty/curve/size flags for the normal flow, the TPM signer for tpmkms, or cryptoutil.CreateSigner for other attestation URIs), finalizes the order, fetches the certificate, and for the TPM signer stores the chain in the TPM via key.SetCertificateChain.

doDeviceAttestation dispatches tpmkms: URIs to doTPMAttestation; for other URIs it uses cryptoutil.CreateAttestor, signs the key authorization (ES256 for P-256 EC, RS256 for RSA, EdDSA for Ed25519, other keys rejected), CBOR-encodes the signature, and posts the attestation payload with the PEM bundle as x5c.

doTPMAttestation parses the tpmkms: attestation URI (parseTPMAttestationURI requires the tpmkms scheme and a name parameter, with optional device and attestation-ca-url), initializes a go.step.sm/crypto/tpm instance with a dirstore at --tpm-storage-directory, maps kty/curve/size to ECDSA 256/384/521 or RSA, and prints TPM info before attesting.

getAK retrieves or creates an attestation key named after the hex fingerprint of the preferred TPM EK (getPreferredEK); if the AK lacks a valid certificate identity (hasValidIdentity checks the EK key-id URI among SANs) it enrolls with the Attestation CA via attestationClient.performAttestation and stores the resulting chain.

The TPM attestation client supports --attestation-ca-root (withRootsFile) and --attestation-ca-insecure options; attestationStatement builds the CBOR attestation object for the 'tpm' format, and attest posts it to the Attestation CA and verifies the decrypted secret.

step ca acme exposes only the eab subcommand group (list, add, remove) which manages ACME External Account Binding Keys on the CA through the admin client; notImplemented converts admin 'not implemented' errors into a message that the functionality is only available in Certificate Manager.

ACME flags are defined in command/ca/ca.go (--acme directory URL, --contact, --http-listen default :80, --standalone, --webroot); --attestation-uri is a shared flag in flags/flags.go documented with tpmkms: URI parameters; step ca certificate additionally defines --attestation-ca-url, --attestation-ca-root, hidden --attestation-ca-insecure, and --tpm-storage-directory (default $(step path)/tpm).

27: // CaClient is the interface implemented by a client used to sign, renew, revoke

30: 	Sign(req *api.SignRequest) (*api.SignResponse, error)

37: 	SSHRekey(req *api.SSHRekeyRequest) (*api.SSHRekeyResponse, error)

44: 	SSHBastion(req *api.SSHBastionRequest) (*api.SSHBastionResponse, error)

50: // NewClient returns a client of an online or offline CA. Requires the flags
51: // `offline`, `ca-config`, `ca-url`, and `root`.
52: func NewClient(ctx *cli.Context, opts ...ca.ClientOption) (CaClient, error) {
53: 	if ctx.Bool("offline") {
54: 		caConfig := ctx.String("ca-config")
55: 		if caConfig == "" {
56: 			return nil, errs.InvalidFlagValue(ctx, "ca-config", "", "")
57: 		}
58: 		return NewOfflineCA(ctx, caConfig)
59: 	}
60: 
61: 	caURL, err := flags.ParseCaURL(ctx)
62: 	if err != nil {
63: 		return nil, err
64: 	}
65: 	root := ctx.String("root")
66: 	if root == "" {
67: 		root = pki.GetRootCAPath()
68: 		if _, err := os.Stat(root); err != nil {
69: 			return nil, errs.RequiredFlag(ctx, "root")
70: 		}
71: 	}
72: 	opts = append([]ca.ClientOption{ca.WithRootFile(root)}, opts...)
73: 	return ca.NewClient(caURL, opts...)
74: }

407: // splitSANs unifies the SAN collections passed as arguments and returns a list

412: 	for _, sans := range args {

416: 				unique = append(unique, san)
417: 			}

238: 		// TODO implement support for replacing the authority section of the
239: 		// URL with placeholders as well.
240: 		apiEndpoint = strings.ReplaceAll(apiEndpoint, "<>", team)
241: 		u, err := url.Parse(apiEndpoint)
242: 		if err != nil {
243: 			return errors.Wrapf(err, "error parsing %s", apiEndpoint)
244: 		}
245: 		apiEndpoint = u.String()
246: 	}
247: 
248: 	// Get the --redirect-url flag, If passed, we will use this one even if the
249: 	// API provides one.
250: 	redirectURL := ctx.String("redirect-url")
251: 	if redirectURL != "" {
252: 		if _, err := url.Parse(redirectURL); err != nil {
253: 			return err
254: 		}
255: 	}
256: 
257: 	// Using public PKI
258: 	//nolint:gosec // Variadic URL is considered safe here for the following reasons:
259: 	//  1) The input is from the command line, rather than a web form or publicly available API.
260: 	//  2) The command is expected to be used on a client, rather than a privileged backend host.

262: 	if err != nil {

264: 	}

266: 	if resp.StatusCode >= 400 {

268: 			return errors.New("error getting authority data: authority not found")
269: 		}
270: 		return errors.Wrap(readError(resp.Body), "error getting authority data")
271: 	}
272: 
273: 	var r bootstrapAPIResponse
274: 	if err := readJSON(resp.Body, &r); err != nil {
275: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "error getting authority data")
276: 	}
277: 	if redirectURL != "" {
278: 		r.RedirectURL = redirectURL
279: 	} else if r.RedirectURL == "" {
280: 		r.RedirectURL = "https://smallstep.com/app/teams/sso/success"
281: 	}
282: 
283: 	bootOpts := []bootstrapOption{
284: 		withDefaultContextValues(teamAuthority + "." + team),
285: 		withRedirectURL(r.RedirectURL),
286: 	}
287: 	if r.Provisioner != "" {
288: 		bootOpts = append(bootOpts, withProvisioner(r.Provisioner))
289: 	}
290: 	if r.MinPasswordLength > 0 {
291: 		bootOpts = append(bootOpts, withMinPasswordLength(r.MinPasswordLength))
292: 	}
293: 	return bootstrap(ctx, r.CaURL, r.Fingerprint, bootOpts...)
294: }

312: 		}

## Objective
- Initialize a complete source-grounded OpenWiki for the SmallStep CLI repository (`/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U`), following the OpenWiki lifecycle through `openwiki_finish`, applying the benchmark brief in `openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md`.

## Important Details
- User constraints: do NOT modify source files; document OpenWiki-generated integration files; do NOT use subagents; do NOT switch models.
- OpenWiki run is `active`: `runId: "422bb7a1-79b8-4652-bc29-ad0dd4ca5f77"`, root `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U`, mode `init`. Plan already SUBMITTED and accepted (13 pages, hierarchical taxonomy with `relatedPages`).
- **OpenWiki Claims contract (learned via tool errors):**
  - For genuinely NEW claims, **omit the `id`** field (including an id on a new claim → error "Claim X is not owned by <path>"). `id` is only reused to confirm/update existing claims.
  - Evidence `resource` values MUST begin with `repo://` and use a repository-relative path, preferably bounded spans `repo://path#L20-L48`; whole-file (`repo://path`) only when the whole file is genuinely the evidence. Bare paths (e.g. `cmd/step/main.go`) are rejected ("Unsupported evidence resource").
  - `openwiki_submit_page` expects the COMPLETE intended Claim set for the assigned page and requires ≥1 material repo-grounded Claim.
  - Page Markdown is written to `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U/openwiki/<subdir>/<file>.md` then submitted.
- Job loop mechanics: `openwiki_next_page({runId})` returns a pending job `{id, path, title, purpose, seedPaths, relatedPages, instructions, status:"pending", mode:"init", existingClaims:[]}`; write the page; `openwiki_submit_page({runId, jobId, claims:[{statement, evidence:[{resource}]}]})` → returns `{status:"complete", page, remaining}`.
- Repo facts (verified): module `github.com/smallstep/cli` (go 1.25.8). Deps: `urfave/cli v1.22.17`, `smallstep/certificates v0.30.2`, `smallstep/cli-utils v0.12.2`, `smallstep/linkedca v0.26.0`, `go.step.sm/crypto v0.89.0`, `smallstep/truststore v0.13.0`, `smallstep/go-attestation` + `google/go-tpm`, `slackhq/nebula v1.10.3`, `pquerna/otp v1.5.0`, `smallstep/zlint`/`zcrypto`, `go-pkcs12`.

# CA Clients and Certificate Request Flows

`utils/cautils` is the core client library that every command which talks to a Step CA is built on. It defines one interface, `CaClient`, with two implementations: an online client (the `smallstep/certificates` API client) and the embedded `OfflineCA`, plus an option-based `CertificateFlow` that builds sign requests and an `admin client` constructor for the management API. A separate bootstrap flow installs the root and default context so later commands work without flags.

## CaClient interface

`CaClient` (utils/cautils/client.go:29-48) is the single surface commands use for CA operations:

- X.509: `Sign`, `Renew`, `RenewWithToken`, `Revoke`, `Rekey`, `Version`, `GetRootCAs`, `GetCaURL`
- SSH: `SSHSign`, `SSHRenew`, `SSHRekey`, `SSHRevoke`, `SSHRoots`, `SSHFederation`, `SSHConfig`, `SSHCheckHost`, `SSHGetHosts`, `SSHBastion`

The online implementation is the `*ca.Client` returned by `ca.NewClient` from `smallstep/certificates`; the offline implementation is `*OfflineCA` below.

### Client construction (client.go:50-204)

- `NewClient(ctx, opts...)` (client.go:52-74) selects the mode from flags:
  - `--offline` requires `--ca-config` and returns `NewOfflineCA(ctx, caConfig)`.
  - Otherwise it resolves the CA URL via `flags.ParseCaURL`, defaults the root to `pki.GetRootCAPath()` (erroring with a required-flag message if missing), prepends `ca.WithRootFile(root)`, and returns `ca.NewClient(caURL, opts...)`.
- `NewUnauthenticatedAdminClient(ctx, opts...)` (client.go:77-96) builds an unauthenticated `*ca.AdminClient` for the management API, requiring `--ca-url` (via `flags.ParseCaURLIfExists`) and the same root resolution.
- `NewAdminClient(ctx, opts...)` (client.go:99-204) builds an authenticated admin client:
  - If `--admin-cert` and `--admin-key` are given (both required together via `errs.RequiredWithFlag`), it loads the cert bundle and key from disk.
  - Otherwise it prints "No admin credentials found. You must login to execute admin commands.", generates a default key, prompts for an admin name/subject unless `--admin-subject` is set, creates a sign token through `NewTokenFlow` (`SignType`), builds a CSR from the subject SANs, signs it with an online client (`ca.NewClient` with the root file), and uses the resulting chain as the admin credentials.
  - In both cases the final client is `ca.NewAdminClient(caURL, ca.WithRootFile(root), ca.WithAdminX5C(adminCert, adminKey, password-file))`.

The `smallstep/certificates` admin API is the linkedca-backed management API; `step ca admin` subcommands additionally use `linkedca` types (e.g. `linkedca.Admin`, `Admin_SUPER_ADMIN`) for admin objects (command/ca/admin/admin.go:69-82).

## CertificateFlow (certificate_flow.go)

`CertificateFlow` (certificate_flow.go:37-40) holds an optional `*OfflineCA` and the `offline` flag. `NewCertificateFlow(ctx, opts...)` (certificate_flow.go:106-131) applies the options and, in offline mode, requires `--ca-config` and constructs the `OfflineCA`.

### Options and flowContext

- `flowContext` (certificate_flow.go:42-48) carries `DisableCustomSANs`, `SSHPublicKey`, `CertificateRequest`, `ConfirmationFingerprint`, and `CustomAttributes`.
- A package-level `sharedContext` (certificate_flow.go:51) is the shared state: all `Option`s are applied to this single struct per process, which is how one command (e.g. `step ca sign` with `--csr`/`--confirm`) passes data to another flow in the same invocation.
- The `Option` interface (certificate_flow.go:67-69) has one method, `apply(fo *flowContext)`. Built-ins, all via `newFuncFlowOption` (certificate_flow.go:53-65): `WithSSHPublicKey` (72-76), `WithCertificateRequest` (79-83), `WithConfirmationFingerprint` (87-91), `WithCustomAttributes` (94-103, merges into the `user` claim map).

### Client selection for a token: `GetClient` (certificate_flow.go:134-171)

- Offline: returns the embedded `OfflineCA` directly.
- Online: parses the OTT with `token.ParseInsecure`.
  - **Bootstrap/provisioning tokens** (payload has a `SHA` claim and an `http(s)` audience): the audience becomes the CA URL when `--ca-url` is unset, and the client trusts the root by fingerprint via `ca.WithRootSHA256(sha)` — no local root file needed.
  - **All other tokens**: `--ca-url` is required, the root defaults to `pki.GetRootCAPath()`, and the client is built with `ca.WithRootFile(root)`.
- Prints the selected CA with `ui.PrintSelected("CA", caURL)`.

### Token generation

- `GenerateToken(ctx, subject, sans)` (certificate_flow.go:176-205): offline → `OfflineCA.GenerateToken` with `SignType`; online → requires `--ca-url` (unless `--token`), resolves the root, prompts "What DNS names or IP addresses would you like to use?" when the subject is empty, then delegates to `NewTokenFlow` (token_flow.go:101).
- `GenerateSSHToken(ctx, subject, typ, principals, validAfter, validBefore)` (certificate_flow.go:209-231): same split, delegating to `NewTokenFlow` with the SSH token type and validity.
- `GenerateIdentityToken(ctx)` (certificate_flow.go:234-247): always online, resolves CA URL/root, and delegates to `NewIdentityTokenFlow` (token_flow.go:187), which builds a token from an OIDC provisioner only.

### Signing a CSR

- `Sign(ctx, tok, csr, crtFile)` (certificate_flow.go:250-293): gets the client via `GetClient`, parses `--not-before`/`--not-after` (`flags.ParseTimeDuration`) and `--template-data` (`flags.ParseTemplateData`), builds `api.SignRequest{CsrPEM, OTT, NotBefore, NotAfter, TemplateData}`, calls `client.Sign`, falls back to `ServerPEM`+`CaPEM` when `CertChainPEM` is empty, serializes the chain, and writes the PEM to `crtFile` with mode `0o600`.
- `CreateSignRequest(ctx, tok, subject, sans)` (certificate_flow.go:297-405) is the helper that produces the `SignRequest` plus the private key:
  - Parses the OTT (`token.ParseInsecure`), derives key details from `--kty`/`--curve`/`--size` (`utils.GetKeyDetailsFromCLI`), and generates the key with `keyutil.GenerateKey`.
  - Merges `--san` values with the token's `sans` claim via `splitSANs` (certificate_flow.go:409-421, deduplicates and classifies with `x509util.SplitSANs`), then applies per-token-type defaults:
    - **AWS**: private IP plus EC2-style internal DNS names.
    - **GCP**: `name.project.c.` and `name.zone.project.c.` internal names.
    - **Azure**: the instance resource name.
    - **OIDC**: if subject equals the token email, CN = token subject, email SAN, and an issuer#subject URI; otherwise CN/SANs from the subject.
    - **K8sSA**: uses the command-line subject (tokens are multi-use).
    - **default**: subject comes from the token.
    - `sharedContext.DisableCustomSANs` suppresses appending the subject to the default cloud SAN lists.
  - Builds the CSR template (`pkix.Name{CommonName: subject}` + SANs), signs and parses it, verifies the signature with `cr.CheckSignature()`, and returns `&api.SignRequest{CsrPEM, OTT}` and the key.

## OfflineCA (offline.go)

`OfflineCA` (offline.go:28-34) wraps a `*authority.Authority` and its `config.Config` from `smallstep/certificates`, letting the CLI perform CA operations with no network.

- **Singleton**: `offlineInstance` (offline.go:36-39) guards `NewOfflineCA` (offline.go:42-81) — double initialization is impossible because the authority backend (badgerDB) holds locks. `NewOfflineCA` reads and unmarshals the `--ca-config` JSON, rejects configs without provisioners, applies `--password-file` to the config password, and calls `authority.New(&cfg)`.
- **Accessors**: `GetCaURL` (84-86, `https://<first DNSName>`), `GetRootCAs` (90-92, always nil), `CaURL` (161-163), `Root` (166-168, first root cert file), `Provisioners` (171-173), `Audience` (141-158, maps token types to `https://<host>/<endpoint>` audiences such as `/sign`, `/renew`, `/revoke`, `/ssh/sign`, ...).
- `VerifyClientCert(certFile, keyFile)` (offline.go:96-138) checks cert/key match via `tls.X509KeyPair` and verifies the cert against the configured root and intermediate pools.
- **Operation wrappers** mirror the `CaClient` interface against `authority.Authority`:
  - `Sign` (offline.go:196-222): authorizes the OTT (`authority.Authorize` with the `provisioner.SignMethod` context), signs with `SignWithContext` (passing `NotBefore`/`NotAfter`/`TemplateData`), and returns the chain (leaf, intermediate) plus the authority's TLS options.
  - `Renew` (226-250): extracts the leaf of the TLS client certificate from the passed `http.Transport` and renews it; `RenewWithToken` (255-275) authorizes a one-time token instead.
  - `Revoke` (279+), `Rekey` (316+), `SSHSign` (345+), `SSHRevoke` (376+), `SSHRenew` (399+), `SSHRekey` (419+), `SSHRoots` (444+), `SSHFederation` (462+) follow the same pattern, and `Version` (185-191) reports the authority version.

## Bootstrap (bootstrap.go)

`bootstrap(ctx, caURL, fingerprint, opts...)` (bootstrap.go:98-222) turns a CA URL + root fingerprint into a working local configuration:

1. Builds an insecure `ca.NewClient` and calls `client.Root(fingerprint)` — the fingerprint check is the trust anchor validation.
2. **Contexts**: when `UseContext` (bootstrap.go:37-42; contexts enabled in config or `--context`/`--authority`/`--profile` set), it adds a context via `step.Contexts().Add` (name defaults to the option's default context, authority/profile default to the name), saves it as current, and sets it. Otherwise it calls `WarnContext` (bootstrap.go:46-54), which prints a hint if a legacy `config/ca.json` exists.
3. Writes the root PEM to `pki.GetRootCAPath()` (typically `$STEPPATH/certs/root_ca.crt`) with mode `0o600`, creating parent dirs with `0o700`.
4. Completes the URL (`utils.CompleteURL`, forcing https) and writes `bootstrapConfig` (ca-url, fingerprint, root, optional redirect-url/provisioner/min-password-length) to `step.DefaultsFile()` (`$STEPPATH/configs/defaults.json`) with mode `0o644`.
5. Sets `ca-url`, `fingerprint`, and `root` back onto the CLI context so the rest of the command can use them.
6. When contexts are enabled, creates an empty profile defaults file (`{}`) if missing.
7. With `--install`, installs the root into the OS truststore via `truststore.InstallFile`.

Two public entry points:

- `BootstrapTeamAuthority(ctx, team, teamAuthority)` (bootstrap.go:226-294): GETs `https://api.smallstep.com/v1/teams/<team>/authorities/<teamAuthority>` (or a custom `--team-url` endpoint with `<team>` substituted for `<>`), parses the `bootstrapAPIResponse` (url, fingerprint, redirect-url, provisioner, min-password-length), defaults the redirect to `https://smallstep.com/app/teams/sso/success`, and runs `bootstrap` with default context name `<teamAuthority>.<team>`. HTTP errors are surfaced through `readError` (bootstrap.go:348-355).
- `BootstrapAuthority(ctx, caURL, fingerprint)` (bootstrap.go:297-317): the plain flow used by `step ca bootstrap`, deriving the default context name from the CA host (`getHost`, bootstrap.go:319-331) or `--authority`, with an optional `--redirect-url`.

## Change guides

### Adding a new CertificateFlow option

1. Add any new state to `flowContext` (utils/cautils/certificate_flow.go:42-48) if the option must carry data.
2. Add a `With...` constructor returning `newFuncFlowOption` (certificate_flow.go:61-65) — the `Option` interface only requires `apply(fo *flowContext)` (certificate_flow.go:67-69).
3. Pass it from the command via `NewCertificateFlow(ctx, With...(...))` or `NewTokenFlow(ctx, ..., With...(...))` (both accept variadic options).

claims.statement: CaClient in utils/cautils/client.go is the single interface commands use for CA operations: X.509 Sign/Renew/RenewWithToken/Revoke/Rekey/Version/GetRootCAs/GetCaURL plus SSH Sign/Renew/Rekey/Revoke/Roots/Federation/Config/CheckHost/GetHosts/Bastion; the online implementation is the *ca.Client from smallstep/certificates and the offline implementation is *cautils.OfflineCA.

NewClient selects the CA mode from flags: --offline requires --ca-config and returns NewOfflineCA(ctx, caConfig); otherwise it resolves the CA URL via flags.ParseCaURL, defaults the root to pki.GetRootCAPath() (required-flag error when missing), prepends ca.WithRootFile, and returns ca.NewClient(caURL, opts...).

NewUnauthenticatedAdminClient builds an unauthenticated *ca.AdminClient for the management API requiring --ca-url; NewAdminClient requires --admin-cert and --admin-key together when given, otherwise prints a 'No admin credentials found' notice, generates a default key, prompts for an admin name/subject unless --admin-subject is set, creates a SignType token via NewTokenFlow, signs a CSR with an online client, and constructs ca.NewAdminClient with ca.WithAdminX5C(adminCert, adminKey, password-file).

CertificateFlow holds an optional *OfflineCA and offline flag; NewCertificateFlow applies the given Options to the package-level sharedContext flowContext and, in offline mode, requires --ca-config and constructs the OfflineCA.

flowContext carries DisableCustomSANs, SSHPublicKey, CertificateRequest, ConfirmationFingerprint and CustomAttributes; the Option interface only requires apply(fo *flowContext), and built-in options (WithSSHPublicKey, WithCertificateRequest, WithConfirmationFingerprint, WithCustomAttributes which merges into the 'user' claim map) are created with newFuncFlowOption; all options are applied to the process-global sharedContext so commands in the same invocation can pass data between flows.

CertificateFlow.GetClient returns the OfflineCA in offline mode; online it parses the OTT and, for bootstrap/provisioning tokens (payload SHA claim plus http audience) uses the audience as the CA URL when --ca-url is unset and trusts the root via ca.WithRootSHA256, while for all other tokens --ca-url is required and the root defaults to pki.GetRootCAPath() with ca.WithRootFile.

GenerateToken (SignType) and GenerateSSHToken delegate to OfflineCA.GenerateToken when offline, otherwise require --ca-url (unless --token), resolve the root, and call NewTokenFlow; GenerateIdentityToken is always online and delegates to NewIdentityTokenFlow, which builds a token using only an OIDC provisioner.

CertificateFlow.Sign gets the client via GetClient, parses --not-before/--not-after and --template-data, builds api.SignRequest{CsrPEM, OTT, NotBefore, NotAfter, TemplateData}, calls client.Sign, falls back to ServerPEM+CaPEM when CertChainPEM is empty, serializes the chain to PEM, and writes the certificate file with mode 0o600.

CreateSignRequest parses the OTT, derives key details from --kty/--curve/--size, generates the key, merges --san values with the token sans claim via splitSANs (dedupe + x509util.SplitSANs), applies per-token-type default SANs (AWS private IP + EC2 internal names, GCP project/zone internal names, Azure resource name, OIDC issuer#subject URI when subject equals the email, K8sSA uses the command-line subject, default uses the token subject), builds and signs a CSR with CommonName from the subject, verifies it with CheckSignature, and returns the SignRequest plus private key; DisableCustomSANs in the shared context suppresses appending the subject to cloud default SANs.

OfflineCA wraps an authority.Authority and its config.Config from smallstep/certificates; NewOfflineCA is guarded by the offlineInstance singleton (double initialization is avoided because the badgerDB-backed authority holds locks), reads and unmarshals the --ca-config JSON, rejects configs without provisioners, applies --password-file, and calls authority.New.

OfflineCA accessors: GetCaURL returns https://<first DNSName>, GetRootCAs always returns nil, CaURL/Root/Provisioners read the config, and Audience maps token types to https://<host>/<endpoint> audiences (/sign, /renew, /revoke, /ssh/sign, /ssh/renew, /ssh/revoke, /ssh/rekey).
OfflineCA.VerifyClientCert checks certificate/key match via tls.X509KeyPair and then verifies the certificate against the configured root and intermediate certificate pools.

OfflineCA.Sign authorizes the OTT with authority.Authorize under a provisioner.SignMethod context and signs with SignWithContext passing NotBefore/NotAfter/TemplateData; Renew extracts the leaf of the TLS client certificate from the passed http.Transport and renews it, while RenewWithToken authorizes a one-time token first; all return the chain (leaf plus intermediate) and the authority TLS options.

OfflineCA also wraps Revoke, Rekey, SSHSign, SSHRevoke, SSHRenew, SSHRekey, SSHRoots and SSHFederation against the corresponding authority.Authority methods, and Version reports the authority version, so the embedded CA satisfies the full CaClient interface.

bootstrap() validates the fingerprint by calling client.Root(fingerprint) on an insecure client; when UseContext is true it adds/sets the step context (authority and profile default to the context name), otherwise WarnContext prints a hint if a legacy config/ca.json exists; it writes the root PEM to pki.GetRootCAPath() with 0o600, writes bootstrapConfig (ca-url, fingerprint, root, optional redirect/provisioner/min-password-length) to step.DefaultsFile() with 0o644, sets ca-url/fingerprint/root on the CLI context, creates an empty profile defaults file when contexts are enabled, and with --install installs the root in the OS truststore.
UseContext returns true when step contexts are enabled in config or --context/--authority/--profile is set; WarnContext advises users to adopt contexts when a legacy config/ca.json is present.

BootstrapTeamAuthority GETs https://api.smallstep.com/v1/teams/<team>/authorities/<teamAuthority> (or a custom --team-url endpoint with <> replaced by the team), parses bootstrapAPIResponse (url, fingerprint, redirect-url, provisioner, min-password-length), defaults the redirect URL to https://smallstep.com/app/teams/sso/success, and runs bootstrap with default context name <teamAuthority>.<team>.

BootstrapAuthority is the plain step ca bootstrap flow: it derives the default context name from the --authority flag or the CA URL host (getHost strips the port), accepts an optional --redirect-url, and runs bootstrap with the given caURL and fingerprint.

The step ca admin package uses linkedca types (linkedca.Admin, Admin_SUPER_ADMIN) together with the *ca.AdminClient for management-API admin objects, e.g. in cliAdmin conversion, listing, and admin prompting.

input.content:
# Provisioner and One-Time Tokens

Commands that talk to a Step CA authenticate with short-lived one-time JWT tokens (OTTs). The CLI builds them in two layers: the `token` package (claim definitions, options, JWT signing/parsing) and `utils/cautils` (the interactive `TokenFlow` that picks a provisioner and per-provisioner `generate*` helpers). The token audience always encodes the CA endpoint it will be presented to, so a token is bound to both the CA URL and the operation (`/1.0/sign`, `/1.0/renew`, ...).

## The token package (token/)

### Constants and claims (token/token.go:11-40)

- `DefaultIssuer = "step-cli"`, `DefaultAudience = "https://ca/sign"` (token/token.go:13-15).
- Validity: `MinValidity = 10s`, `DefaultValidity = 5m`, `MaxValidity = 1h`, `MaxValidityDelay = 30m` (token/token.go:17-23).
- Step CA custom claim names: `sha` (root SHA-256), `sans` (required SANs), `step` (certificate custom info), `user` (user-provided custom info), `cnf` (confirmation / proof-of-possession) (token/token.go:26-40).

`Claims` (token/token.go:48-52) wraps `jose.Claims` with `ExtraClaims`/`ExtraHeaders` maps; `DefaultClaims` (token/token.go:118-130) seeds issuer, default audience, and a 5-minute validity from `time.Now()`; `Sign` (token/token.go:71-104) builds a JOSE signer with `kid` (via `GenerateKeyID`, the SHA-256 thumbprint of the public key, token/token.go:132-144) and compact-serializes the JWT, forcing `aud` to a string when there is a single audience.

### Options (token/options.go)

`Options` is a function `func(*Claims) error` (token/options.go:27-28). Key constructors:

- Identity/claims: `WithClaim` (31), `WithIssuer` (172), `WithSubject` (184), `WithAudience` (196), `WithJWTID` (208), `WithKid` (220, overrides the thumbprint kid).
- Step CA claims: `WithRootCA` (45, computes the `sha` claim from a root file), `WithSHA` (59), `WithSANS` (68), `WithStep` (76), `WithUserData` (85, merges into `user`), `WithSSH` (104, sets `step` with `provisioner.SignSSHOptions`), `WithConfirmationFingerprint` (112) and `WithFingerprint` (123, builds `cnf` from a CSR).
- Validity: `WithValidity` (148, validates boundaries against Min/MaxValidity).
- Headers: `WithX5CFile`/`WithX5CCerts` (231/247, sets the `x5c` header), `WithNebulaCert` (261, sets the nebula header), `WithX5CInsecureCerts` (319+, sets `x5cAllowInvalid` for self-signed chains).

### Parsing (token/parse.go)

- `Parse(token, key)` (token/parse.go:139-151) verifies the signature; `ParseInsecure(token)` (token/parse.go:154-166) reads claims without verification — the flow uses `ParseInsecure` because signature verification is the CA's job.
- `Payload` (token/parse.go:38-62) decodes standard JWT claims plus Step CA claims: `sha`/`sans` (JWK tokens), `at_hash`/`azp`/`email`/... (OIDC), Azure claims (`appid`, `tid`, `xms_mirid`, ...), Kubernetes service-account claims (`kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/*`), and embedded GCP/AWS/Azure identity payloads.
- `Payload.Type()` (token/parse.go:65-82) classifies tokens: GCP (`google` claim) → AWS (`amazon`) → Azure → K8sSA (issuer `kubernetes/serviceaccount`) → JWK (`sha` or `sans` present) → OIDC (aud/iss/sub/exp/iat set) → `Unknown`.
- `parseResponse` (token/parse.go:168-189) post-processes AWS documents (unmarshals the instance identity document) and Azure tokens (matches `xms_mirid` against `azureXMSMirIDRegExp` and checks known Azure issuer prefixes, token/parse.go:191-206).

### provision.Token (token/provision/provision.go:14-35)

`provision.Token` is the unsigned one-time token type used by the generators: `New(subject, opts...)` starts from `token.WithSubject` + defaults, and `SignedString(sigAlg, key)` compact-serializes it. Unlike a bootstrap token it does not self-contain networking information for reaching the CA.

## TokenFlow (utils/cautils/token_flow.go)

### Sign types and audiences

Eight token signing types (utils/cautils/token_flow.go:26-36): `SignType`, `RevokeType`, `SSHUserSignType`, `SSHHostSignType`, `SSHRevokeType`, `SSHRenewType`, `SSHRekeyType`, `RenewType`.

`parseAudience` (utils/cautils/token_flow.go:39-76) maps each type to an endpoint path under the CA URL (scheme forced to https): `/1.0/sign`, `/1.0/renew`, `/1.0/revoke`, `/1.0/ssh/sign` (both SSH sign types), `/1.0/ssh/revoke`, `/1.0/ssh/renew`, `/1.0/ssh/rekey`; other schemes are rejected.

### NewTokenFlow (utils/cautils/token_flow.go:101-183)

1. Applies flow options to the shared context.
2. Builds the audience; for `RenewType` it skips provisioner discovery entirely and calls `generateRenewToken` (an x5c-based renewal token).
3. Otherwise fetches provisioners with `pki.GetProvisioners(caURL, root)` (smallstep/certificates) and runs `provisionerPrompt`.
4. Prompts for the subject when empty — skipped for OIDC provisioners (the CA derives principals from the email), with a different prompt for `SSHUserSignType` ("What user principal would you like to use? (e.g. alice)").
5. Dispatches on the provisioner concrete type:
   - `JWK` → `generateJWKToken`
   - `OIDC` → `generateOIDCToken`
   - `X5C` → `generateX5CToken`
   - `Nebula` → `generateNebulaToken`
   - `SSHPOP` → `generateSSHPOPToken`
   - `K8sSA` → `generateK8sSAToken`
   - `GCP`/`AWS`/`Azure` → `p.GetIdentityToken(subject, caURL)` after copying the provisioner's `DisableCustomSANs` into the shared context
   - `ACME` → `&ACMETokenError{Name}` ("step ACME provisioners do not support token auth flows", utils/cautils/token_flow.go:78-87); `SCEP` → `&SCEPTokenError` (utils/cautils/token_flow.go:89-98)

`ACMETokenError` is consumed by `step ca certificate` to switch into the ACME flow with the provisioner name (command/ca/certificate.go:258-266).

### NewIdentityTokenFlow (utils/cautils/token_flow.go:187-205)

The bootstrap flow: lists only OIDC provisioners (filter on `provisioner.TypeOIDC`), prompts, and calls `generateOIDCToken`; any other type is an error.

### OfflineTokenFlow (utils/cautils/token_flow.go:212-273)

Used with `--offline`. If the `--ca-config` file exists it delegates to `OfflineCA.GenerateToken`; otherwise it requires `--provisioner`/`--issuer` plus `--key` (with optional `--kid`), derives the audience and root the same way, and generates an X5C token when `--x5c-cert`/`--x5c-key` is set, else a JWK token.

### provisionerPrompt (utils/cautils/token_flow.go:291-408)

- Flag-driven type filters: `--x5c-cert`/`--x5c-key` → only X5C; `--sshpop-cert`/`--sshpop-key` → only SSHPOP; `--nebula-cert`/`--nebula-key` → only Nebula; `--k8ssa-token-path` → only K8sSA; default lists JWK, OIDC, ACME, SCEP, K8sSA, X5C, SSHPOP, Nebula and cloud (GCP/AWS/Azure) provisioners.
- Extra filters: `--kid` matches `JWK.Key.KeyID` or `OIDC.ClientID`; `--admin-provisioner` and `--provisioner`/`--issuer` match by name. Each mismatch is an `errs.InvalidFlagValue`.
- Renders items per type (e.g. `name (type) [kid: ...]`, `[client: ...]`, `[tenant: ...]`); a single candidate is auto-selected and printed, otherwise `ui.Select` prompts "What provisioner key do you want to use?".

## Token generators (utils/cautils/token_generator.go)

`TokenGenerator` (utils/cautils/token_generator.go:35-53) holds `kid`, `iss`, `aud`, `root`, validity times, and the signing `jwk`:

- `Token(sub, opts...)` (utils/cautils/token_generator.go:56-94): random 256-bit `jti` to catch duplicates, `WithKid`/`WithIssuer`/`WithAudience`, `WithRootCA` when a root is set, optional `WithValidity`, then `provision.New` + `SignedString` with the JWK's algorithm.
- `SignToken` (utils/cautils/token_generator.go:98-117): adds `WithSANS` (subject as the only SAN when empty), ties the request to the CSR via `WithFingerprint` (from `sharedContext.CertificateRequest`) or `WithConfirmationFingerprint`, and merges `sharedContext.CustomAttributes` into `user`.
- `RevokeToken` (120-122) is plain; `SignSSHToken` (125-140) adds `WithSSH` with `CertType`, `KeyID` (subject), `Principals`, and `ValidAfter`/`ValidBefore`.

Per-provisioner generators:

- `generateJWKToken` (utils/cautils/token_generator.go:441-469) + `loadJWK` (380-439): the key comes from `--key` (loaded via `cryptoutil.LoadJSONWebKey`, KMS-aware) or from the CA — offline mode uses the provisioner's `encryptedKey` from ca.json, online mode fetches `pki.GetProvisionerKey(caURL, root, kid)`; the encrypted JWK is decrypted with a prompted password and unmarshaled. The issuer is the provisioner name. Dispatches by token type to `SignToken`/`RevokeToken`/`SignSSHToken` (user/host).
- `generateOIDCToken` (utils/cautils/token_generator.go:144-169): execs the CLI's own `step oauth --oidc --bare` with the provisioner's `ConfigurationEndpoint`, `ClientID`, `ClientSecret`, scopes/auth-params, optional `--console`, and `--listen` from `ListenAddress` (unless `STEP_LISTEN` is set), returning the token on stdout.
- `generateX5CToken` (utils/cautils/token_generator.go:195-273): requires `--x5c-cert`/`--x5c-key`, builds a KMS-aware signer (`cryptoutil.CreateSigner`), picks the JOSE algorithm with `getSigningAlgorithm` (ES256/384/512, RSA default, EdDSA; utils/cautils/token_generator.go:519-539), appends `--x5c-chain` certs, sets the `x5c` header (or `x5cAllowInvalid` with `--x5c-insecure`), and uses audience `<aud>#<provisioner ID>` via `p.GetIDForToken()`.
- `generateNebulaToken` (utils/cautils/token_generator.go:275-311): reads the nebula signing key with `jose.ReadKey` (ed25519 CA key), audience `<aud>#<provisioner ID>`, and sets the nebula header via `token.WithNebulaCert`.
- `generateSSHPOPToken` (utils/cautils/token_generator.go:313-345): only supports `SSHRevokeType`/`SSHRenewType`/`SSHRekeyType` with `--sshpop-cert`/`--sshpop-key`, attaching the SSH cert via `token.WithSSHPOPFile`.
- `generateK8sSAToken` (utils/cautils/token_generator.go:183-193): reads the service account token from `--k8ssa-token-path` (default `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token`) and returns it as-is.
- `generateRenewToken` (utils/cautils/token_generator.go:471-517): requires `--x5c-cert`/`--x5c-key`, verifies the subject argument matches the leaf CN when given, builds claims with issuer `step-ca-client/1.0` and the target audience, sets the x5c chain in `ExtraHeaders[jose.X5cInsecureKey]`, and signs with the leaf key.

## Where audience/fingerprint derivation happens

- Audience: `parseAudience` (utils/cautils/token_flow.go:39-76) for token-flow tokens; per-provisioner generators append `#<provisioner ID>` for X5C/Nebula/SSHPOP. Bootstrap/provisioning tokens carry the root as the `sha` claim (`token.WithRootCA`, token/options.go:45) and `CertificateFlow.GetClient` uses that SHA to trust the CA (utils/cautils/certificate_flow.go:134-171).
- Fingerprinting: `token.WithFingerprint` (token/options.go:123) derives the `cnf` claim from a CSR in the shared flow context; `GenerateKeyID` (token/token.go:132-144) derives `kid` as a SHA-256 JWK thumbprint.
- Uncertainty: token *verification*, provisioner key retrieval (`pki.GetProvisioners`, `pki.GetProvisionerKey`), and identity-token validation live inside `smallstep/certificates` (and `go.step.sm/crypto/jose` for JOSE mechanics); this repository only constructs, parses, and presents tokens.

claims.statement: The token package defines DefaultIssuer 'step-cli', DefaultAudience 'https://ca/sign', validity bounds MinValidity 10s / DefaultValidity 5m / MaxValidity 1h / MaxValidityDelay 30m, and the Step CA claim names sha (root SHA256), sans, step, user, and cnf (confirmation/proof-of-possession).

Claims wraps jose.Claims with ExtraClaims/ExtraHeaders; DefaultClaims seeds issuer, default audience and a 5-minute validity from time.Now(); Sign builds a JOSE signer with kid set to the SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the public key (GenerateKeyID) and compact-serializes the JWT, forcing aud to a string for single audiences.

Options is func(*Claims) error; constructors include WithClaim, WithRootCA (computes the sha claim from a root file), WithSHA, WithSANS, WithStep, WithUserData (merges into the user claim), WithSSH (sets the step claim with provisioner.SignSSHOptions), WithConfirmationFingerprint, and WithFingerprint (builds the cnf claim from a CSR), plus WithValidity which validates boundaries against the Min/Max validity constants.

token/options.go also provides WithIssuer, WithSubject, WithAudience, WithJWTID, WithKid (overrides the thumbprint kid), WithX5CFile/WithX5CCerts (set the x5c header), and WithNebulaCert (sets the nebula header); WithX5CInsecureCerts sets x5cAllowInvalid for self-signed chains.

token/parse.go defines the token Type enum (JWK, X5C, OIDC, GCP, AWS, Azure, K8sSA, Nebula) and Payload, which decodes standard claims plus sha/sans (JWK), at_hash/azp/email (OIDC), Azure claims, kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/* claims, and embedded GCP/AWS/Azure identity payloads; Payload.Type() classifies by google claim, amazon claim, Azure issuer, kubernetes/serviceaccount issuer, sha or sans presence, then OIDC-like standard claims.

Parse verifies the token signature with the given key while ParseInsecure reads claims without verification; parseResponse unmarshals the AWS instance identity document and parses Azure xms_mirid with a case-insensitive regex limited to known Azure issuer prefixes.

provision.Token is the unsigned one-time token used by the generators: New(subject, opts...) starts from WithSubject plus default claims and SignedString compact-serializes the JWT; unlike a bootstrap token it does not self-contain networking information for reaching the CA.

TokenFlow defines eight signing types (SignType, RevokeType, SSHUserSignType, SSHHostSignType, SSHRevokeType, SSHRenewType, SSHRekeyType, RenewType) and parseAudience maps them to /1.0/sign, /1.0/renew, /1.0/revoke, /1.0/ssh/sign (both SSH sign types), /1.0/ssh/revoke, /1.0/ssh/renew, /1.0/ssh/rekey under the CA URL with the scheme forced to https, rejecting other schemes.

NewTokenFlow applies flow options, builds the audience, skips provisioner discovery for RenewType (generateRenewToken), otherwise fetches provisioners via pki.GetProvisioners and prompts; it prompts for the subject unless the provisioner is OIDC (or SSH user sign uses a principal prompt), then dispatches JWK/OIDC/X5C/Nebula/SSHPOP/K8sSA to their generators, GCP/AWS/Azure to p.GetIdentityToken after copying DisableCustomSANs, and returns ACMETokenError or SCEPTokenError (carrying the provisioner name) for those provisioner types.
NewIdentityTokenFlow is the bootstrap flow: it filters to OIDC provisioners only, prompts, and calls generateOIDCToken, erroring for any other provisioner type.

OfflineTokenFlow with --offline delegates to OfflineCA.GenerateToken when the --ca-config file exists, otherwise requires --provisioner/--issuer and --key (with optional --kid), derives the audience and root, and generates an X5C token when --x5c-cert/--x5c-key is set, otherwise a JWK token.

provisionerPrompt filters provisioners by flags (--x5c-cert/--x5c-key to X5C, --sshpop-* to SSHPOP, --nebula-* to Nebula, --k8ssa-token-path to K8sSA; default lists JWK/OIDC/ACME/SCEP/K8sSA/X5C/SSHPOP/Nebula and cloud types), then by --kid (JWK KeyID or OIDC ClientID), --admin-provisioner, and --provisioner/--issuer by name, rendering per-type labels and auto-selecting a single candidate or prompting with ui.Select.

TokenGenerator (kid, iss, aud, root, validity, jwk) provides Token (random 256-bit jti, WithKid/WithIssuer/WithAudience, WithRootCA when a root is set, optional WithValidity, provision.New + SignedString with the JWK algorithm), SignToken (WithSANS defaulting to the subject, WithFingerprint from the shared-context CSR or WithConfirmationFingerprint, user attributes), RevokeToken, and SignSSHToken (WithSSH with cert type, key id, principals, and validity).

generateJWKToken uses loadJWK to obtain the signing JWK: from --key via cryptoutil.LoadJSONWebKey (KMS-aware), or from the CA — the provisioner encryptedKey from ca.json in offline mode or pki.GetProvisionerKey(caURL, root, kid) online — decrypted with a prompted password; the issuer is the provisioner name and the token type dispatches to SignToken/RevokeToken/SignSSHToken (user or host).

generateOIDCToken execs the CLI's own 'step oauth --oidc --bare' with the provisioner ConfigurationEndpoint, ClientID, ClientSecret, scopes and auth params, optional --console, and --listen from the provisioner ListenAddress unless STEP_LISTEN is set, returning the token on stdout; generateK8sSAToken reads the service account token from --k8ssa-token-path (default /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token) and returns it unchanged.

generateX5CToken requires --x5c-cert/--x5c-key, builds a KMS-aware signer, picks the JOSE algorithm via getSigningAlgorithm (ES256/384/512, RSA default, EdDSA; other keys error), appends --x5c-chain certs, sets the x5c header (or x5cAllowInvalid with --x5c-insecure), and uses audience <aud>#<provisioner ID>; generateNebulaToken reads the ed25519 CA key with jose.ReadKey and sets the nebula header with the same audience pattern; generateSSHPOPToken only supports SSH revoke/renew/rekey types with --sshpop-cert/--sshpop-key via token.WithSSHPOPFile.

generateRenewToken requires --x5c-cert/--x5c-key, verifies the subject argument matches the leaf common name when given, builds claims with issuer 'step-ca-client/1.0' and the target audience, sets the x5c chain in ExtraHeaders[jose.X5cInsecureKey], and signs with the leaf key.

Audience derivation happens in parseAudience (endpoint path from the CA URL plus token type) with per-provisioner generators appending '#<provisioner ID>'; bootstrap/provisioning tokens instead carry the root as the sha claim via token.WithRootCA, and CertificateFlow.GetClient uses that SHA to trust the CA (ca.WithRootSHA256) when the audience is an http URL.

Token verification, provisioner listing, and provisioner key retrieval (pki.GetProvisioners, pki.GetProvisionerKey) are performed inside the external smallstep/certificates package; the CLI only constructs, parses, and presents tokens, so its behavior there is delegated rather than implemented in this repository.

package ca

import (
	"github.com/urfave/cli"

	"github.com/smallstep/cli-utils/command"

	"github.com/smallstep/cli/command/ca/acme"
	"github.com/smallstep/cli/command/ca/admin"
	"github.com/smallstep/cli/command/ca/policy"
	"github.com/smallstep/cli/command/ca/provisioner"
)

// init creates and registers the ca command
func init() {
	cmd := cli.Command{
		Name:      "ca",
		Usage:     "initialize and manage a certificate authority",
		UsageText: "**step ca** <subcommand> [arguments] [global-flags] [subcommand-flags]",
		Description: `**step ca** command group provides facilities to initialize a certificate
authority, retrieve the root of trust, sign and renew certificates, and create
and manage provisioners.

## EXAMPLES

Create the configuration for a new certificate authority:
'''
$ step ca init
'''

Configure the ca-url and root in the environment:
'''
$ step ca bootstrap \
  --ca-url https://ca.smallstep.com \
  --fingerprint 0d7d3834cf187726cf331c40a31aa7ef6b29ba4df601416c9788f6ee01058cf3
$ cat $STEPPATH/config/defaults.json
{
  "ca-url": "https://ca.smallstep.com",
  "fingerprint": "0d7d3834cf187726cf331c40a31aa7ef6b29ba4df601416c9788f6ee01058cf3",
  "root": "/home/user/.step/certs/root_ca.crt"
}
'''

Download the root_ca.crt:
'''
$ step ca root root_ca.crt \
  --ca-url https://ca.smallstep.com \
  --fingerprint 0d7d3834cf187726cf331c40a31aa7ef6b29ba4df601416c9788f6ee01058cf3
'''

Get the Health status of the CA:
'''
$ step ca health --ca-url https://ca.smallstep.com --root /home/user/.step/certs/root_ca.crt
'''

Create a new certificate using a token:
'''
$ TOKEN=$(step ca token internal.example.com)
$ step ca certificate internal.example.com internal.crt internal.key \
  --token $TOKEN --ca-url https://ca.smallstep.com --root root_ca.crt
'''

Renew a certificate (certificate must still be valid):
'''
$ step ca renew internal.crt internal.key \
  --ca-url https://ca.smallstep.com --root root_ca.crt
'''`,
		Subcommands: cli.Commands{
			healthCommand(),
			initCommand(),

65: The **--daemon** flag can be combined with **--pid**, **--signal**, or **--exec**
66: to provide certificate reloads on your services.
67: 
68: By default, the renew command authenticates to step-ca using mTLS, except when
69: the certificate is expired and renewal after expiry is allowed by the CA.
70: 
71: There are scenarios where mTLS is not possible: When step-ca is behind a layer 7 proxy,
72: when the server's leaf certificate EKU is not configured for client authentication,
73: or when the server is a StepCAS RA for an upstream step-ca server.
74: For these scenarios, use **--mtls=false** to force a flow that uses X5C
75: token-based authentication.
76: 
77: ## POSITIONAL ARGUMENTS
78: 
79: <crt-file>
80: :  The certificate in PEM format that we want to renew.
81: 
82: <key-file>
83: :  They key file of the certificate.
84: 
85: ## EXAMPLES
86: 
87: Renew a certificate with the configured CA:
88: '''
89: $ step ca renew internal.crt internal.key
90: Would you like to overwrite internal.crt [Y/n]: y
91: '''
92: 
93: Renew a certificate without overwriting the previous certificate:
94: '''
95: $ step ca renew --out renewed.crt internal.crt internal.key
96: '''
97: 
98: Renew a certificate forcing the overwrite of the previous certificate:
99: '''
100: $ step ca renew --force internal.crt internal.key
101: '''
102: 
103: Renew a certificate using the token flow instead of mTLS:
104: '''
105: $ step ca renew --mtls=false --force internal.crt internal.key
106: '''
107: 
108: Renew a certificate which key is in a KMS:
109: '''
110: $ step ca renew yubikey.crt 'yubikey:slot-id=9a?pin-value=123456'
111: '''
112: 
113: Renew a certificate which key is in a KMS, using the <--kms> flag:
114: '''
115: $ step ca renew \
116:   --kms 'pkcs11:module-path=/usr/local/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so;token=smallstep?pin-value=password' \
117:   pkcs11.crt 'pkcs11:id=4001'
118: '''
119: 
120: Renew a certificate providing the <--ca-url> and <--root> flags:
121: '''
122: $ step ca renew --ca-url https://ca.smallstep.com:9000 \
123:   --root /path/to/root_ca.crt internal.crt internal.key
124: Would you like to overwrite internal.crt [Y/n]: y
125: '''
126: 
127: Renew skipped because it was too early:
128: '''
129: $ step ca renew --expires-in 8h internal.crt internal.key
130: certificate not renewed: expires in 10h52m5s
131: '''
132: 
133: Renew the certificate before 2/3 of the validity has passed:
134: '''
135: $ step ca renew --daemon internal.crt internal.key
136: '''
137: 
138: Renew the certificate before 8 hours and 30m of the expiration time:
139: '''
140: $ step ca renew --daemon --expires-in 8h30m internal.crt internal.key
141: '''
142: 
143: Renew the certificate every 16h:
144: '''
145: $ step ca renew --daemon --renew-period 16h internal.crt internal.key
146: '''
147: 
148: Renew the certificate and reload nginx:
149: '''
150: $ step ca renew --daemon --exec "nginx -s reload" internal.crt internal.key
151: '''
152: 
153: Renew the certificate and convert it to DER:
154: '''
155: $ step ca renew --daemon --renew-period 16h \
156:   --exec "step certificate format --force --out internal.der internal.crt" \
157:   internal.crt internal.key
158: '''
159: 
160: Renew a certificate using the offline mode, requires the configuration
161: files, certificates, and keys created with **step ca init**:
162: '''
163: $ step ca renew --offline internal.crt internal.key
164: '''`,
165: 		Flags: []cli.Flag{
166: 			cli.BoolTFlag{
167: 				Name: "mtls",
168: 				Usage: `Use mTLS to renew a certificate. Use --mtls=false to force the token
169: authorization flow instead.`,
170: 			},
171: 			flags.CaConfig,
172: 			flags.Force,
173: 			flags.Offline,
174: 			flags.PasswordFile,
175: 			flags.KMSUri,
176: 			cli.StringFlag{
177: 				Name:  "out,output-file",
178: 				Usage: "The new certificate <file> path. Defaults to overwriting the <crt-file> positional argument",
179: 			},
180: 			cli.StringFlag{
181: 				Name: "expires-in",
182: 				Usage: `The amount of time remaining before certificate expiration,
183: at which point a renewal should be attempted. The certificate renewal will not
184: be performed if the time to expiration is greater than the **--expires-in** value.
185: A random jitter (duration/20) will be added to avoid multiple services hitting the
186: renew endpoint at the same time. The <duration> is a sequence of decimal numbers,
187: each with optional fraction and a unit suffix, such as "300ms", "-1.5h" or "2h45m".
188: Valid time units are "ns", "us" (or "µs"), "ms", "s", "m", "h".`,
189: 			},
190: 			cli.IntFlag{
191: 				Name: "pid",
192: 				Usage: `The process id to signal after the certificate has been renewed. By default the
193: the SIGHUP (1) signal will be used, but this can be configured with the **--signal**
194: flag.`,
195: 			},
196: 			cli.StringFlag{
197: 				Name: "pid-file",
198: 				Usage: `The <file> from which to read the process id that will be signaled after the certificate
199: has been renewed. By default the SIGHUP (1) signal will be used, but this can be configured with the **--signal**
200: flag.`,
201: 			},
202: 			cli.IntFlag{
203: 				Name: "signal",
204: 				Usage: `The signal <number> to send to the selected PID, so it can reload the
205: configuration and load the new certificate. Default value is SIGHUP (1)`,
206: 				Value: int(syscall.SIGHUP),
207: 			},
208: 			cli.StringFlag{
209: 				Name:  "exec",
210: 				Usage: "The <command> to run after the certificate has been renewed.",
211: 			},
212: 			cli.BoolFlag{
213: 				Name: "daemon",
214: 				Usage: `Run the renew command as a daemon, renewing and overwriting the certificate
215: periodically. By default the daemon will renew a certificate before 2/3 of the
216: time to expiration has elapsed. The period can be configured using the
217: **--renew-period** or **--expires-in** flags.`,
218: 			},
219: 			cli.StringFlag{
220: 				Name: "renew-period",
221: 				Usage: `The period with which to schedule renewals of the certificate in daemon mode.
222: Requires the **--daemon** flag. The <duration> is a sequence of decimal numbers,
223: each with optional fraction and a unit suffix, such as "300ms", "1.5h", or "2h45m".
224: Valid time units are "ns", "us" (or "µs"), "ms", "s", "m", "h".`,
225: 			},
226: 			flags.CaURL,
227: 			flags.Root,
228: 			flags.Context,
229: 		},
230: 	}
231: }

233: func renewCertificateAction(ctx *cli.Context) error {
234: 	err := errs.NumberOfArguments(ctx, 2)
235: 	if err != nil {
236: 		return err
237: 	}
238: 
239: 	args := ctx.Args()
240: 	certFile := args.Get(0)
241: 	keyFile := args.Get(1)
242: 	passFile := ctx.String("password-file")
243: 	isDaemon := ctx.Bool("daemon")
244: 	execCmd := ctx.String("exec")
245: 	kmsURI := ctx.String("kms")
246: 
247: 	outFile := ctx.String("out")
248: 	if outFile == "" {
249: 		outFile = certFile
250: 	}
251: 
252: 	rootFile := ctx.String("root")
253: 	if rootFile == "" {
254: 		rootFile = pki.GetRootCAPath()
255: 	}
256: 
257: 	caURL, err := flags.ParseCaURL(ctx)
258: 	if err != nil {
259: 		return err
260: 	}
261: 
262: 	var expiresIn, renewPeriod time.Duration
263: 	if s := ctx.String("expires-in"); s != "" {
264: 		if expiresIn, err = time.ParseDuration(s); err != nil {
265: 			return errs.InvalidFlagValue(ctx, "expires-in", s, "")
266: 		}
267: 	}
268: 	if s := ctx.String("renew-period"); s != "" {
269: 		if renewPeriod, err = time.ParseDuration(s); err != nil {
270: 			return errs.InvalidFlagValue(ctx, "renew-period", s, "")
271: 		}
272: 	}
273: 	if expiresIn > 0 && renewPeriod > 0 {
274: 		return errs.IncompatibleFlagWithFlag(ctx, "expires-in", "renew-period")
275: 	}
276: 	if renewPeriod > 0 && !isDaemon {
277: 		return errs.RequiredWithFlag(ctx, "renew-period", "daemon")
278: 	}
279: 
280: 	if ctx.IsSet("pid") && ctx.IsSet("pid-file") {
281: 		return errs.MutuallyExclusiveFlags(ctx, "pid", "pid-file")
282: 	}
283: 	pid := ctx.Int("pid")
284: 	if ctx.IsSet("pid") && pid <= 0 {
285: 		return errs.InvalidFlagValue(ctx, "pid", strconv.Itoa(pid), "")
286: 	}
287: 
288: 	pidFile := ctx.String("pid-file")
289: 	if pidFile != "" {
290: 		pidB, err := os.ReadFile(pidFile)
291: 		if err != nil {
292: 			return errs.FileError(err, pidFile)
293: 		}
294: 		pid, err = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(string(pidB)))
295: 		if err != nil {
296: 			return errs.Wrap(err, "error converting %s to integer process id", pidB)
297: 		}
298: 		if pid <= 0 {
299: 			return errs.InvalidFlagValue(ctx, "pid-file", strconv.Itoa(pid), "")
300: 		}
301: 	}
302: 
303: 	signum := ctx.Int("signal")
304: 	if ctx.IsSet("signal") && signum <= 0 {
305: 		return errs.InvalidFlagValue(ctx, "signal", strconv.Itoa(signum), "")
306: 	}
307: 
308: 	cert, err := tlsLoadX509KeyPair(kmsURI, certFile, keyFile, passFile)
309: 	if err != nil {
310: 		return err
311: 	}
312: 
313: 	cvp := cert.Leaf.NotAfter.Sub(cert.Leaf.NotBefore)
314: 	if renewPeriod > 0 && renewPeriod >= cvp {
315: 		return errors.Errorf("flag '--renew-period' must be within (lower than) the certificate "+
316: 			"validity period; renew-period=%v, cert-validity-period=%v", renewPeriod, cvp)
317: 	}
318: 	if expiresIn > cvp {
319: 		return errors.Errorf("flag '--expires-in' must be within (lower than) the certificate "+
320: 			"validity period; expires-in=%v, cert-validity-period=%v", expiresIn, cvp)
321: 	}
322: 
323: 	renewer, err := newRenewer(ctx, caURL, cert, rootFile)
324: 	if err != nil {
325: 		return err
326: 	}
327: 
328: 	afterRenew := getAfterRenewFunc(pid, signum, execCmd)
329: 	if isDaemon {
330: 		// Force is always enabled when daemon mode is used
331: 		ctx.Set("force", "true")
332: 		next := nextRenewDuration(cert.Leaf, expiresIn, renewPeriod)
333: 		return renewer.Daemon(outFile, next, expiresIn, renewPeriod, afterRenew)
334: 	}
335: 
336: 	// Do not renew if (cert.notAfter - now) > (expiresIn + jitter)
337: 	if expiresIn > 0 {
338: 		//nolint:gosec // The random number below is not being used for crypto.
339: 		jitter := rand.Int63n(int64(expiresIn / 20))
340: 		if d := time.Until(cert.Leaf.NotAfter); d > expiresIn+time.Duration(jitter) {
341: 			ui.Printf("certificate not renewed: expires in %s\n", d.Round(time.Second))
342: 			return nil
343: 		}
344: 	}
345: 
346: 	if _, err := renewer.Renew(outFile); err != nil {
347: 		return err
348: 	}
349: 
350: 	ui.Printf("Your certificate has been saved in %s.\n", outFile)
351: 	return afterRenew()
352: }
353: 
354: func nextRenewDuration(leaf *x509.Certificate, expiresIn, renewPeriod time.Duration) time.Duration {
355: 	if renewPeriod > 0 {
356: 		// Renew now if it will be expired in renewPeriod
357: 		if (time.Until(leaf.NotAfter) - renewPeriod) <= 0 {
358: 			return 0
359: 		}
360: 		return renewPeriod
361: 	}
362: 
363: 	period := leaf.NotAfter.Sub(leaf.NotBefore)
364: 	if expiresIn == 0 {
365: 		expiresIn = period / 3
366: 	}
367: 
368: 	switch d := time.Until(leaf.NotAfter) - expiresIn; {
369: 	case d <= 0:
370: 		return 0
371: 	case d < period/20:
372: 		//nolint:gosec // The random number below is not being used for crypto.
373: 		return time.Duration(rand.Int63n(int64(d)))
374: 	default:
375: 		//nolint:gosec // The random number below is not being used for crypto.
376: 		n := rand.Int63n(int64(period / 20))
377: 		d -= time.Duration(n)
378: 		return d
379: 	}
380: }
381: 
382: func getAfterRenewFunc(pid, signum int, execCmd string) func() error {
383: 	return func() error {
384: 		if err := runKillPid(pid, signum); err != nil {
385: 			return err
386: 		}
387: 		return runExecCmd(execCmd)
388: 	}
389: }
390: 
391: func runKillPid(pid, signum int) error {
392: 	if pid == 0 {
393: 		return nil
394: 	}
395: 	if err := sysutils.Kill(pid, syscall.Signal(signum)); err != nil {
396: 		return errors.Wrapf(err, "kill %d with signal %d failed", pid, signum)
397: 	}
398: 	return nil
399: }
400: 
401: func runExecCmd(execCmd string) error {
402: 	execCmd = strings.TrimSpace(execCmd)
403: 	if execCmd == "" {
404: 		return nil
405: 	}
406: 	parts := strings.Split(execCmd, " ")
407: 	//nolint:gosec // arguments controlled by step.
408: 	cmd := exec.Command(parts[0], parts[1:]...)
409: 	cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
410: 	cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
411: 	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
412: 	return cmd.Run()
413: }

415: type renewer struct {
416: 	client    cautils.CaClient
417: 	transport *http.Transport
418: 	key       crypto.PrivateKey
419: 	offline   bool
420: 	cert      tls.Certificate
421: 	caURL     *url.URL
422: 	mtls      bool
423: }

425: func newRenewer(ctx *cli.Context, caURL string, cert tls.Certificate, rootFile string) (*renewer, error) {
426: 	if len(cert.Certificate) == 0 {
427: 		return nil, errors.New("error loading certificate: certificate chain is empty")
428: 	}
429: 
430: 	rootCAs, err := x509util.ReadCertPool(rootFile)
431: 	if err != nil {
432: 		return nil, err
433: 	}
434: 
435: 	tr := &http.Transport{
436: 		Proxy: http.ProxyFromEnvironment,
437: 		TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{
438: 			RootCAs:                  rootCAs,
439: 			PreferServerCipherSuites: true,
440: 			MinVersion:               tls.VersionTLS12,
441: 		},
442: 	}
443: 
444: 	if time.Now().Before(cert.Leaf.NotAfter) {
445: 		tr.TLSClientConfig.Certificates = []tls.Certificate{cert}
446: 	}
447: 
448: 	var client cautils.CaClient
449: 	offline := ctx.Bool("offline")
450: 	if offline {
451: 		caConfig := ctx.String("ca-config")
452: 		if caConfig == "" {
453: 			return nil, errs.InvalidFlagValue(ctx, "ca-config", "", "")
454: 		}
455: 		client, err = cautils.NewOfflineCA(ctx, caConfig)
456: 		if err != nil {
457: 			return nil, err
458: 		}
459: 	} else {
460: 		client, err = ca.NewClient(caURL, ca.WithTransport(tr))
461: 		if err != nil {
462: 			return nil, err
463: 		}
464: 	}
465: 
466: 	u, err := url.Parse(client.GetCaURL())
467: 	if err != nil {
468: 		return nil, errors.Errorf("error parsing CA URL: %s", client.GetCaURL())
469: 	}
470: 
471: 	return &renewer{
472: 		client:    client,
473: 		transport: tr,
474: 		key:       cert.PrivateKey,
475: 		offline:   offline,
476: 		cert:      cert,
477: 		caURL:     u,
478: 		mtls:      ctx.Bool("mtls"),
479: 	}, nil
480: }
481: 
482: func (r *renewer) Renew(outFile string) (resp *api.SignResponse, err error) {
483: 	if !r.mtls || time.Now().After(r.cert.Leaf.NotAfter) {
484: 		resp, err = r.RenewWithToken(r.cert)
485: 	} else {
486: 		resp, err = r.client.Renew(r.transport)
487: 	}
488: 	if err != nil {
489: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error renewing certificate")
490: 	}
491: 
492: 	if len(resp.CertChainPEM) == 0 {
493: 		resp.CertChainPEM = []api.Certificate{resp.ServerPEM, resp.CaPEM}
494: 	}
495: 	var data []byte
496: 	for _, certPEM := range resp.CertChainPEM {
497: 		pemblk, err := pemutil.Serialize(certPEM.Certificate)
498: 		if err != nil {
499: 			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error serializing certificate PEM")
500: 		}
501: 		data = append(data, pem.EncodeToMemory(pemblk)...)
502: 	}
503: 	if err := fileutil.WriteFile(outFile, data, 0o600); err != nil {
504: 		return nil, errs.FileError(err, outFile)
505: 	}
506: 
507: 	return resp, nil
508: }

510: func (r *renewer) Rekey(priv interface{}, outCert, outKey string, writePrivateKey bool) (*api.SignResponse, error) {
511: 	csrBytes, err := x509.CreateCertificateRequest(cryptoRand.Reader, &x509.CertificateRequest{}, priv)
512: 	if err != nil {
513: 		return nil, err
514: 	}
515: 	csr, err := x509.ParseCertificateRequest(csrBytes)
516: 	if err != nil {
517: 		return nil, err
518: 	}
519: 	resp, err := r.client.Rekey(&api.RekeyRequest{CsrPEM: api.NewCertificateRequest(csr)}, r.transport)
520: 	if err != nil {
521: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error rekeying certificate")
522: 	}
523: 	if len(resp.CertChainPEM) == 0 {
524: 		resp.CertChainPEM = []api.Certificate{resp.ServerPEM, resp.CaPEM}
525: 	}
526: 	var data []byte
527: 	for _, certPEM := range resp.CertChainPEM {
528: 		pemblk, err := pemutil.Serialize(certPEM.Certificate)
529: 		if err != nil {
530: 			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error serializing certificate PEM")
531: 		}
532: 		data = append(data, pem.EncodeToMemory(pemblk)...)
533: 	}
534: 	if err := fileutil.WriteFile(outCert, data, 0o600); err != nil {
535: 		return nil, errs.FileError(err, outCert)
536: 	}
537: 	if writePrivateKey {
538: 		_, err = pemutil.Serialize(priv, pemutil.ToFile(outKey, 0o600))
539: 		if err != nil {
540: 			return nil, err
541: 		}
542: 	}
543: 
544: 	return resp, nil
545: }

547: // RenewAndPrepareNext renews the cert and prepares the cert for it's next renewal.
548: // NOTE: this function logs each time the certificate is successfully renewed.
549: func (r *renewer) RenewAndPrepareNext(outFile string, expiresIn, renewPeriod time.Duration) (time.Duration, error) {
550: 	const durationOnErrors = 1 * time.Minute
551: 	infoLog := log.New(os.Stdout, "INFO: ", log.LstdFlags)
552: 
553: 	resp, err := r.Renew(outFile)
554: 	if err != nil {
555: 		return durationOnErrors, err
556: 	}
557: 
558: 	x509Chain, err := pemutil.ReadCertificateBundle(outFile)
559: 	if err != nil {
560: 		return durationOnErrors, errs.Wrap(err, "error reading certificate chain")
561: 	}
562: 	x509ChainBytes := make([][]byte, len(x509Chain))
563: 	for i, c := range x509Chain {
564: 		x509ChainBytes[i] = c.Raw
565: 	}
566: 
567: 	cert := tls.Certificate{
568: 		Certificate: x509ChainBytes,
569: 		PrivateKey:  r.key,
570: 		Leaf:        x509Chain[0],
571: 	}
572: 	if len(cert.Certificate) == 0 {
573: 		return durationOnErrors, errors.New("error loading certificate: certificate chain is empty")
574: 	}
575: 
576: 	// Prepare next transport
577: 	r.cert = cert
578: 	r.transport.TLSClientConfig.Certificates = []tls.Certificate{cert}
579: 
580: 	// Get next renew duration
581: 	next := nextRenewDuration(resp.ServerPEM.Certificate, expiresIn, renewPeriod)
582: 	infoLog.Printf("%s certificate renewed, next in %s", resp.ServerPEM.Certificate.Subject.CommonName, next.Round(time.Second))
583: 	return next, nil
584: }
585: 
586: func (r *renewer) Daemon(outFile string, next, expiresIn, renewPeriod time.Duration, afterRenew func() error) error {
587: 	// Loggers
588: 	infoLog := log.New(os.Stdout, "INFO: ", log.LstdFlags)
589: 	errLog := log.New(os.Stderr, "ERROR: ", log.LstdFlags)
590: 
591: 	// Daemon loop
592: 	signals := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
593: 	signal.Notify(signals, syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM, syscall.SIGHUP)
594: 	defer signal.Stop(signals)
595: 
596: 	infoLog.Printf("first renewal in %s", next.Round(time.Second))
597: 	var err error
598: 	for {
599: 		select {
600: 		case sig := <-signals:
601: 			switch sig {
602: 			case syscall.SIGHUP:
603: 				if next, err = r.RenewAndPrepareNext(outFile, expiresIn, renewPeriod); err != nil {
604: 					errLog.Println(err)
605: 				} else if err := afterRenew(); err != nil {
606: 					errLog.Println(err)
607: 				}
608: 			case syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM:
609: 				return nil
610: 			}
611: 		case <-time.After(next):
612: 			if next, err = r.RenewAndPrepareNext(outFile, expiresIn, renewPeriod); err != nil {
613: 				errLog.Println(err)
614: 			} else if err := afterRenew(); err != nil {
615: 				errLog.Println(err)
616: 			}
617: 		}
618: 	}
619: }

621: // RenewWithToken creates an authorization token with the given certificate and
622: // attempts to renew the given certificate. It can be used to renew expired
623: // certificates.
624: func (r *renewer) RenewWithToken(cert tls.Certificate) (*api.SignResponse, error) {
625: 	claims, err := token.NewClaims(
626: 		token.WithAudience(r.caURL.ResolveReference(&url.URL{Path: "/renew"}).String()),
627: 		token.WithIssuer("step-ca-client/1.0"),
628: 		token.WithSubject(cert.Leaf.Subject.CommonName),
629: 	)
630: 	if err != nil {
631: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error creating authorization token")
632: 	}
633: 	var x5c []string
634: 	for _, b := range cert.Certificate {
635: 		x5c = append(x5c, base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(b))
636: 	}
637: 	if claims.ExtraHeaders == nil {
638: 		claims.ExtraHeaders = make(map[string]interface{})
639: 	}
640: 	claims.ExtraHeaders[jose.X5cInsecureKey] = x5c
641: 
642: 	tok, err := claims.Sign("", cert.PrivateKey)
643: 	if err != nil {
644: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error signing authorization token")
645: 	}
646: 
647: 	// Remove existing certificate from the transport. And close keep-alive

657: 	x509Chain, err := pemutil.ReadCertificateBundle(certFile)
658: 	if err != nil {
659: 		return tls.Certificate{}, errs.Wrap(err, "error reading certificate chain")
660: 	}

662: 	for i, c := range x509Chain {

part.text:
## Objective
- Initialize a complete source-grounded OpenWiki for the SmallStep CLI repository (`/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U`), following the OpenWiki lifecycle through `openwiki_finish`, applying the benchmark brief in `openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md`.

## Important Details
- User constraints: do NOT modify source files; document OpenWiki-generated integration files; do NOT use subagents; do NOT switch models.
- OpenWiki run is `active`: `runId: "422bb7a1-79b8-4652-bc29-ad0dd4ca5f77"`, root `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U`, mode `init`. Plan already SUBMITTED and accepted (13 pages, hierarchical taxonomy with `relatedPages`).
- **OpenWiki Claims contract (learned via tool errors):**
  - For genuinely NEW claims, **omit the `id`** field (`id` is only reused to confirm/update existing claims).
  - Evidence `resource` values MUST begin with `repo://` and use a repository-relative path, preferably bounded spans `repo://path#L20-L48`; whole-file only when genuinely the whole file is the evidence. Bare paths are rejected.
  - Spans must actually resolve: a span extending past EOF (e.g. `repo://command/ca/acme/eab/eab.go#L52-L90` when the file is 89 lines) is rejected with "Evidence does not resolve". Always `wc -l` / `grep -n` to verify line numbers before citing.
  - `openwiki_submit_page` expects the COMPLETE intended Claim set for the assigned page and requires ≥1 material repo-grounded Claim.
  - Page Markdown is written to `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U/openwiki/<subdir>/<file>.md` then submitted.
- Job loop mechanics: `openwiki_next_page({runId})` → pending job `{id, path, title, purpose, seedPaths, relatedPages, instructions, status:"pending", mode:"init", existingClaims:[]}`; write page; `openwiki_submit_page({runId, jobId, claims:[{statement, evidence:[{resource}]}]})` → `{status:"complete", page, remaining}`.
- Repo facts (verified): module `github.com/smallstep/cli` (go 1.25.8). Deps: `urfave/cli v1.22.17`, `smallstep/certificates v0.30.2`, `smallstep/cli-utils v0.12.2`, `smallstep/linkedca v0.26.0`, `go.step.sm/crypto v0.89.0`, `smallstep/truststore v0.13.0`, `smallstep/go-attestation`+`google/go-tpm`, `slackhq/nebula v1.10.3`, `pquerna/otp v1.5.0`, `smallstep/zlint`/`zcrypto`, `go-pkcs12`.
- Architecture (verified): entry `cmd/step/main.go` (`step.Set`, `ca.UserAgent`, `cmd.SetName`, `cmd.Run()`) → `internal/cmd/root.go` `Run()`/`run()`; commands self-register via `init()`+`command.Register`; enabled via blank imports (api, base64, beta, ca, certificate, completion, context, crl, crypto, fileserver, oauth, path, ssh) + CAS; plugin `step-<name>-plugin` (only `kms`→step-kms-plugin).
- Two CA modes: online `CaClient` (utils/cautils/client.go `NewClient`) vs offline `--offline`+`--ca-config` → `OfflineCA` singleton wrapping `authority.Authority` (utils/cautils/offline.go).
- Build: Makefile `all: lint test build`, `ci: test build`, `make bootstrap`, `make build`→`bin/`, CGO_ENABLED=0; LDFLAGS `-X main.Version/BuildTime`.

## Work State
### Completed
- `openwiki_begin` (active/planning); extensive repo research; `openwiki_submit_plan` ACCEPTED (13 pages).
- **Page 1 complete**: `/openwiki/architecture/command-framework.md` (job `7b3be2b3-...`) — 13 claims; `remaining:12`.
- **Page 2 complete**: `/openwiki/architecture/overview.md` (job `bc8e4563-...`) — 8 claims; `remaining:11`.
- **Page 3 complete**: `/openwiki/ca-integration/acme-and-tpm.md` (job `f5d55a9b-e5a1-4f45-9a37-f1a810032412`). First submit failed (eab.go span past EOF); corrected `command/ca/acme/eab/eab.go` span to `#L45-L89` (file is 89 lines; `Command()` L45, `notImplemented` L81) and resubmitted → `remaining:10`.
- **Page 4 complete**: `/openwiki/ca-integration/ca-client-and-flows.md` (job `eacd95a3-05ad-4eb7-924a-21f10ffc5330`) — 19 claims; `remaining:9`. Documented `CaClient` interface (client.go L29-48), `NewClient` (L52-74), admin clients (L77-204), `CertificateFlow`/`flowContext`/`sharedContext`/`Option` (certificate_flow.go L37-131), `GetClient` bootstrap-vs-normal token trust (L134-171), `Sign`/`CreateSignRequest` (L250-421), `OfflineCA` (offline.go L28-481), `bootstrap` (bootstrap.go L98-222, L226-294, L297-331), and linkedca usage in `command/ca/admin/admin.go` L69-82.
- **Page 5 complete**: `/openwiki/ca-integration/provisioner-tokens.md` (job `b08f82f5-08db-4827-9dbf-23e41a79ea78`) — 18 claims; `remaining:8`. Documented token package (token.go L11-144, options.go, parse.go, provision.go), `TokenFlow` (token_flow.go: 8 sign types L26-36, `parseAudience` L39-76, `NewTokenFlow` L101-183, `NewIdentityTokenFlow` L187-205, `OfflineTokenFlow` L212-273, `provisionerPrompt` L291-408), and `TokenGenerator` + `generate*` per-provisioner (token_generator.go L33-539).

### Active
- **Page 6 in progress**: `/openwiki/commands/ca.md` (job `392d3b95-f0ec-4a65-ae4e-9d56cd4ec87d`). Page NOT yet written; claims NOT yet submitted. Investigation so far:
  - Directory listing: `command/ca/` = {acme/, admin/, bootstrap.go, ca.go, certificate.go, federation.go, health.go, init.go, policy/, provisioner/, rekey.go, renew.go, revoke.go, root.go, sign.go, token.go} (+ tests). `command/ca/admin/` = {add.go, admin.go, list.go, remove.go, update.go}. `command/ca/policy/` = {acme/, actions/, authority/, policy.go, policycontext/, provisioner/, ssh/, x509/}. `command/ca/policy/actions/` = {cn.go, dns.go, emails.go, ips.go, policy.go, principals.go, remove.go, uris.go, view.go, wildcards.go}. `command/ca/provisioner/` = {add.go, caConfigClient.go, getEncryptedKey.go, list.go, provisioner.go, remove.go, update.go, webhook/}.
  - **`command/beta/` contains only `beta.go` (25 lines) — there is NO `command/beta/ca/` subdirectory** (the plan's seedPaths assumed one). `beta.go` registers `ca.BetaCommand()`.
  - Command names/line anchors from grep: `health.go` `healthCommand()` L17, `healthAction` L57; `init.go` `initCommand()` L33 (flags root/key/key-password-file/pki/ssh/helm/deployment-type/name/dns/address/provisioner); `token.go` `tokenCommand()` L23 (flags san/principal/not-before/not-after/key/output-file/revoke/renew/rekey/ssh, `tokenAction` L282); `certificate.go` `certificateCommand()` L21 (flags san + attestation-* + tpm-storage-directory, `certificateAction` L220); `rekey.go` `rekeyCertificateCommand()` L27 (flags out-cert/out-key/private-key/expires-in/pid/pid-file/signal/exec/daemon/rekey-period, `rekeyCertificateAction` L234).
  - `command/ca/ca.go` `init()` registers `cli.Command{Name:"ca",...}` with subcommands and shared flags (acme/contact/http-listen/standalone/webroot/fingerprint/kid/host).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Finish investigating `command/ca.md` seeds: grep/read `renew.go` (daemon mode: `RenewAndPrepareNext`, `nextRenewDuration`, after-renew hook kill-pid/exec-cmd, systemd timer), `revoke.go`, `sign.go`, `root.go` (root + roots), `federation.go`, `bootstrap.go`; `provisioner/provisioner.go`+`add`/`list`/`update`/`remove`+`webhook/`; `admin/admin.go`+`add`/`list`/`remove`/`update` (linkedca admin client, admin-provisioner/admin-subject/admin-password-file/admin-cert/admin-key); `policy/policy.go`+`actions/*.go` (x509/ssh allow+deny actions); and `ca.BetaCommand()`.
2. Write `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U/openwiki/commands/ca.md`, then `openwiki_submit_page({runId:"422bb7a1-79b8-4652-bc29-ad0dd4ca5f77", jobId:"392d3b95-f0ec-4a65-ae4e-9d56cd4ec87d", claims:[ ...NO `id` fields, all verified `repo://#Lx-Ly` spans... ]})` → expect `remaining:7`.
3. Continue the job loop for the 7 remaining pages (`quickstart.md`, `configuration/environment.md`, `commands/certificate.md`, `commands/ssh.md`, `commands/crypto.md`, `operations/distribution-and-renewal.md`, `development/build-test-and-change-guides.md` — order per OpenWiki): `openwiki_next_page` → research with native tools → write page → `openwiki_submit_page`.
4. Call `openwiki_finish` once all 13 pages are complete.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U/openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md`: benchmark brief (architecture, ownership, flows, config, failure handling, quickstart + change guides, source citations, uncertainty, non-overlapping taxonomy).
- `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U/openwiki/{architecture/command-framework.md, architecture/overview.md, ca-integration/acme-and-tpm.md, ca-integration/ca-client-and-flows.md, ca-integration/provisioner-tokens.md}`: pages 1–5, complete.
- `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U/command/ca/ca.go`: `step ca` group registration + shared flags (current page core).
- `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U/command/ca/{token,certificate,rekey,renew,revoke,sign,root,federation,health,init,bootstrap}.go`: `step ca` leaf subcommands to document (renew daemon mode is a named instruction).
- `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U/command/ca/provisioner/` (+ `webhook/`): provisioner CRUD + webhook subcommands.
- `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U/command/ca/admin/` (add/list/remove/update/admin.go): admin management via linkedca `*ca.AdminClient` (linkedca types at admin.go L69-82).
- `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U/command/ca/policy/` (+ `actions/`): policy authority/provisioner/acme with x509/ssh allow+deny.
- `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U/command/beta/beta.go`: beta group, registers `ca.BetaCommand()` (no `ca/` subdir exists).
- `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U/utils/cautils/{client,certificate_flow,token_flow,offline,bootstrap,acme_flow,acmeutils,tpm,token_generator}.go`, `token/*.go`, `flags/flags.go`: CA-integration pages (done).
- `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U/cmd/step/main.go`, `internal/cmd/root.go`, `internal/plugin/plugin.go`, `internal/command/inject.go`, `Makefile`, `go.mod`, `command/README.md`: architecture pages (done).
- `/tmp/openwiki-bench-ExSe2U/{internal/sshutil,command/{certificate,ssh,crypto,context},systemd,docker,debian,powershell,integration,docs/local-development.md,CONTRIBUTING.md}`: seeds for remaining pages.
